blocks.zh: 第三章：水質選項與系統規劃
blocks.en: Chapter 3: Water Quality Options and System Planning

blocks.zh: 本節學習目標 Learning Objectives
blocks.en: Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 理解製藥用水的品質階層：Drinking Water（飲用水）、Non-Compendial Water（非藥典水）、Purified Water（純化水）、WFI（注射用水），以及各自的適用場景。
blocks.en: Understand the quality hierarchy of pharmaceutical water: Drinking Water, Non-Compendial Water, Purified Water (PW) and Water for Injection (WFI), and where each is appropriate.

blocks.zh: 掌握 USP 藥典水與非藥典水的差異，說明何時可使用非藥典水以及需要什麼文件支持。
blocks.en: Understand the difference between USP compendial water and non-compendial water, and explain when non-compendial water may be used and what documentation supports it.

blocks.zh: 認識不同水質選項的成本影響因素，包含 NPV（淨現值）分析方法。
blocks.en: Recognize the factors that drive the cost of the different water quality options, including the NPV (net present value) analysis method.

blocks.zh: 掌握 ISPE 四步驟系統規劃方法論：確定水質 → 特徵化使用點 → 建立系統標準 → 重新檢視水質。
blocks.en: Master the four-step ISPE system planning methodology: define water quality, characterize the use points, establish system criteria, then revisit water quality.

blocks.zh: 能夠解讀 Use-Point Criteria（使用點標準）矩陣，包含 Diversity Factor（多樣性因子）的概念與應用。
blocks.en: Be able to interpret the Use-Point Criteria matrix, including the concept and application of the Diversity Factor.

blocks.zh: 理解系統設計中 Central System（集中式系統）與 Multiple Systems（分散式系統）的優缺點比較。
blocks.en: Understand the advantages and disadvantages of a Central System versus Multiple Systems in system design.

blocks.zh: 章節導覽 Section Navigator
blocks.en: Section Navigator

blocks.zh: 教學解析 Commentary
blocks.en: Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念：本章定位
blocks.en: Core Concept: Where This Chapter Fits

blocks.zh: 本章是整個 ISPE Vol.4 的「策略起點」。在進入具體的前處理（Chapter 4）、純化技術（Chapter 5-6）、儲存配送（Chapter 7-8）之前，你必須先回答兩個根本問題：
blocks.en: This chapter is the "strategic starting point" of ISPE Vol.4. Before getting into pretreatment (Chapter 4), purification technologies (Chapters 5-6) and storage and distribution (Chapters 7-8), you must first answer two fundamental questions:

blocks.zh: 需要什麼品質的水？ — Water Quality Options（水質選項）
blocks.en: What quality of water is needed? - Water Quality Options

blocks.zh: 用什麼系統來供應？ — System Configurations（系統配置）
blocks.en: What kind of system will supply it? - System Configurations

blocks.zh: 這兩個問題的答案決定了後續所有技術決策的基調。
blocks.en: The answers to these two questions set the tone for every technical decision that follows.

blocks.zh: 生活比喻
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy

blocks.zh: 想像你要為一棟大樓規劃供水。你不會直接去買水管和水泵，而是先問：「住戶需要飲用水、熱水還是軟水？」以及「要一個中央供水站，還是每層樓各裝一套？」— 這就是本章在做的事：先定策略，再選技術。
blocks.en: Imagine planning the water supply for a building. You would not go straight out and buy pipes and pumps. You would first ask: "Do the residents need drinking water, hot water or softened water?" and "Do we want one central water station, or a separate unit on each floor?" That is what this chapter does: set the strategy first, then choose the technology.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：Decision Tree
blocks.en: Key Point: The Decision Tree

blocks.zh: 本章提供的 Decision Tree（決策樹，Figure 3-1）是選水的核心工具。它會根據你的產品類型（口服、注射、外用）、製程特性（有無滅菌步驟、濃縮步驟）來引導你選擇適當的水質等級。每個選擇都需要 QA 審核和文件支持。
blocks.en: The Decision Tree provided in this chapter (Figure 3-1) is the core tool for selecting water. It guides you to an appropriate water grade based on your product type (oral, injectable, topical) and process characteristics (presence of a sterilization step or a concentration step). Every choice requires QA review and documentary support.

blocks.zh: 核心概念：水質需求的三大驅動因素
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Three Drivers of Water Quality Requirements

blocks.zh: 選擇製藥用水品質的起點是三個因素：
blocks.en: The starting point for selecting pharmaceutical water quality is three factors:

blocks.zh: Product Characteristics（產品特性） — 注射劑 vs. 口服劑 vs. 外用品，風險等級不同
blocks.en: Product Characteristics - injectables vs. orals vs. topicals carry different levels of risk

blocks.zh: Manufacturing Processes（製造流程） — 是否有後續的滅菌、純化步驟
blocks.en: Manufacturing Processes - whether there are subsequent sterilization or purification steps

blocks.zh: Intended Use（預期用途） — 大容量靜脈注射 vs. 小劑量口服
blocks.en: Intended Use - large-volume intravenous injection vs. low-dose oral products

blocks.zh: 這三者共同決定了你需要的最低水質標準。
blocks.en: Together, these three determine the minimum water quality standard you need.

blocks.zh: 關鍵洞察：USP 是「最低要求」不是「最佳做法」
blocks.en: Key Insight: USP Is a "Minimum Requirement", Not "Best Practice"

blocks.zh: 原文明確指出：USP Monographs（美國藥典專論）定義的是 minimum requirements（最低要求）。這意味著：
blocks.en: The source text states clearly that USP Monographs define minimum requirements. This means:

blocks.zh: 符合 USP 不等於一定安全 — 特定產品可能需要更嚴格的標準
blocks.en: Complying with USP does not automatically mean the water is safe - a particular product may need a stricter standard

blocks.zh: 不符合 USP 不等於一定不行 — 如果有充分的科學依據和文件支持，製造商可以制定自己的水質標準
blocks.en: Not complying with USP does not automatically mean the water cannot be used - with sound scientific justification and documentation, a manufacturer may set its own water quality standard

blocks.zh: 關鍵是：你必須能證明你的選擇是合理的
blocks.en: The key point: you must be able to demonstrate that your choice is justified

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：一水多用 vs. 分級供水
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: One Water for Everything vs. Graded Supply

blocks.zh: 想像一間餐廳：如果只有一個水龍頭，那它必須供應最乾淨的水（因為要同時用來煮湯和洗碗）。但如果你有兩個水龍頭（一個給廚房、一個給洗碗），你可以針對不同用途優化水質和成本。
blocks.en: Imagine a restaurant. With only one tap, it must supply the cleanest water (because it is used both for cooking soup and for washing dishes). With two taps (one for the kitchen, one for dishwashing), you can optimize water quality and cost for each use.

blocks.zh: 藥廠也一樣：小藥廠通常只做一個水質等級（最高標準全場通用），大藥廠則會分級供水以節省成本。
blocks.en: Drug manufacturers face the same choice: small plants usually run a single water grade (the highest standard everywhere), while large plants use graded supply to save cost.

blocks.zh: CDMO 實務應用
blocks.en: CDMO Practice

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO（委託開發暨製造組織）來說，這個「分級 vs. 統一」的決策格外重要：
blocks.en: For a CDMO (contract development and manufacturing organization), this "graded vs. unified" decision is especially important:

blocks.zh: 多客戶產品組合 — CDMO 同時生產多種客戶產品，水質需求可能差異很大
blocks.en: Multi-client portfolio - a CDMO makes many clients' products at the same time, and their water quality needs can differ widely

blocks.zh: 彈性考量 — 如果只裝一套 WFI 系統，所有產品都用 WFI，成本高但驗證簡單
blocks.en: Flexibility - installing a single WFI system and using WFI for every product costs more but keeps validation simple

blocks.zh: 成本考量 — 如果裝 PW + WFI 雙系統，運維複雜但長期省錢
blocks.en: Cost - installing separate PW and WFI systems is more complex to operate and maintain but saves money over the long term

blocks.zh: 實務建議 — 以無菌充填為核心業務的 CDMO，通常傾向全場 WFI，因為客戶審計時最容易通過
blocks.en: Practical recommendation - a CDMO whose core business is aseptic filling usually leans toward WFI throughout the facility, because it is the easiest position to defend in client audits

blocks.zh: 核心概念：製藥用水的三大分類
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Three Categories of Pharmaceutical Water

blocks.zh: ISPE 將製藥用水分為三個層次，由低到高：
blocks.en: ISPE divides pharmaceutical water into three tiers, from lowest to highest:

blocks.zh: WFI（注射用水）— 最嚴格
blocks.en: WFI (Water for Injection) - the most stringent

blocks.zh: PW / Compendial Water（純化水 / 藥典水）
blocks.en: PW / Compendial Water (Purified Water / compendial water)

blocks.zh: Non-Compendial Water（非藥典水：RO 水、DI 水等）
blocks.en: Non-Compendial Water (e.g. RO water, DI water)

blocks.zh: Drinking Water（飲用水）— 基本門檻
blocks.en: Drinking Water - the basic threshold

blocks.zh: 常見誤解：非藥典水 ≠ 低品質水
blocks.en: Common Misconception: Non-Compendial Water Is Not Low-Quality Water

blocks.zh: 原文特別強調：Non-compendial water is not necessarily less critical, or less costly.
blocks.en: The source text specifically stresses: Non-compendial water is not necessarily less critical, or less costly.

blocks.zh: 非藥典水只是說它不需要完全符合 USP 專論的所有測試項目，但它可能：
blocks.en: Non-compendial water simply means it does not need to meet every test in a USP monograph, but it may be:

blocks.zh: 純度比 PW 更高（例如 RO/DI/UF 三段處理的水）
blocks.en: Higher in purity than PW (for example, water from a three-stage RO/DI/UF treatment)

blocks.zh: 驗證成本不一定更低（因為要自訂標準並提供科學依據）
blocks.en: Not necessarily cheaper to validate (because you must define your own specification and provide the scientific justification)

blocks.zh: 命名方式是依最終處理步驟命名：RO Water、DI Water、UF Water 等
blocks.en: Named after its final treatment step: RO Water, DI Water, UF Water, and so on

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：Decision Tree = 點餐流程
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: The Decision Tree Is Like Ordering a Meal

blocks.zh: Decision Tree 就像餐廳的點餐引導：
blocks.en: The Decision Tree works like a restaurant's ordering process:

blocks.zh: 「您要正餐還是飲料？」→ Production use vs. Lab use
blocks.en: "Would you like a main course or a drink?" → Production use vs. Lab use

blocks.zh: 「正餐是要牛排還是沙拉？」→ Parenteral product vs. Oral product
blocks.en: "Steak or salad for the main course?" → Parenteral product vs. Oral product

blocks.zh: 「牛排要幾分熟？」→ WFI vs. PW vs. Non-compendial
blocks.en: "How would you like the steak cooked?" → WFI vs. PW vs. Non-compendial

blocks.zh: 每一步都是基於你的需求來縮小選項，最終得到最適合的水質。但注意：如果你在藥品申請文件（Drug Application）中已承諾使用特定水質，那個承諾優先於 Decision Tree 的建議。
blocks.en: Each step narrows the options based on your needs until you arrive at the most suitable water quality. But note: if you have already committed to a specific water quality in your Drug Application, that commitment takes precedence over the Decision Tree's recommendation.

blocks.zh: Decision Tree 六大備註的實務意義
blocks.en: Practical Meaning of the Six Decision Tree Notes

blocks.zh: 這六條備註揭示了幾個關鍵原則：
blocks.en: These six notes reveal several key principles:

blocks.zh: Note 1-2（實驗室）：分析方法本身可能要求藥典水；cGMP 實驗室一律走 cGMP 路徑
blocks.en: Notes 1-2 (laboratory): the analytical method itself may require compendial water; a cGMP laboratory always follows the cGMP path

blocks.zh: Note 3（非藥典 ≠ 低質）：非藥典水可以比藥典水更純，重點是控制 Endotoxin（內毒素）和微生物
blocks.en: Note 3 (non-compendial is not low quality): non-compendial water can be purer than compendial water; the focus is on controlling endotoxin and microorganisms

blocks.zh: Note 4（最終清洗）：如果後續有 Sanitization（消毒）步驟，最終沖洗可用非藥典水
blocks.en: Note 4 (final rinse): if a subsequent sanitization step follows, non-compendial water may be used for the final rinse

blocks.zh: Note 6（API）：非無菌注射級 API 的最終純化步驟需要 WFI 級內毒素標準
blocks.en: Note 6 (API): the final purification step of a non-sterile injectable-grade API requires WFI-level endotoxin standards

blocks.zh: 核心概念：選擇水處理系統的三大評估標準
blocks.en: Core Concept: Three Criteria for Evaluating a Water Treatment System

blocks.zh: Suitable Specification（合適的規格） — 水質必須滿足產品和製程需求
blocks.en: Suitable Specification - the water quality must meet product and process needs

blocks.zh: Consistent Quality（一致的品質） — 系統必須能穩定產出相同品質的水
blocks.en: Consistent Quality - the system must reliably produce water of the same quality

blocks.zh: Monitoring KPI（監控關鍵指標） — 必須有方法確認水質持續合格
blocks.en: Monitoring KPI - there must be a way to confirm that the water quality remains acceptable

blocks.zh: 技術比較：常見水處理配置
blocks.en: Technical Comparison: Common Water Treatment Configurations

blocks.zh: 從上表可以歸納出幾個關鍵技術組合：
blocks.en: The table above yields several key technology combinations:

blocks.zh:
前處理（共通）：Primary Filtration → Softening → Carbon Filtration
  ├─ RO 路線：RO (Single/Double Pass)
  │    ├─ + DI (Mixed Bed)  = RO/DI Water
  │    ├─ + EDI             = RO/EDI Water ← 現代主流
  │    └─ + DI + UF         = RO/DI/UF Water
  ├─ DI 路線：Ion Exchange (Two Stage)
  │    └─ + UF              = DI/UF Water
  └─ 蒸餾路線：Still        = Distilled Water
blocks.en:
Pretreatment (common): Primary Filtration → Softening → Carbon Filtration
  ├─ RO route: RO (Single/Double Pass)
  │    ├─ + DI (Mixed Bed)  = RO/DI Water
  │    ├─ + EDI             = RO/EDI Water ← modern mainstream
  │    └─ + DI + UF         = RO/DI/UF Water
  ├─ DI route: Ion Exchange (Two Stage)
  │    └─ + UF              = DI/UF Water
  └─ Distillation route: Still        = Distilled Water

blocks.zh: RO/EDI（逆滲透＋電去離子）是目前業界最主流的 PW 製造方案，因為它不需要化學再生、維護簡單、運行成本低。
blocks.en: RO/EDI (reverse osmosis plus electrodeionization) is currently the most common PW production solution in industry, because it needs no chemical regeneration, is simple to maintain and has low running costs.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：Table 3-1 的正確解讀方式
blocks.en: Key Point: How to Read Table 3-1 Correctly

blocks.zh: 這張表不是「從左到右越好」的排序，而是「不同路徑的技術組合」。選擇哪種組合取決於：
blocks.en: This table is not a ranking that gets "better from left to right". It lists "technology combinations along different routes". Which combination to choose depends on:

blocks.zh: 進水水質（TDS 總溶解固體、硬度、有機物）
blocks.en: Feed water quality (TDS - total dissolved solids, hardness, organics)

blocks.zh: 出水規格（PW 或 WFI）
blocks.en: Product water specification (PW or WFI)

blocks.zh: 工廠條件（是否有化學品操作許可、人員能力、空間）
blocks.en: Site conditions (permits to handle chemicals, staff capability, space)

blocks.zh: 經濟考量（資本支出 vs. 運營成本）
blocks.en: Economics (capital expenditure vs. operating cost)

blocks.zh: 思考練習
blocks.en: Thought Exercise

blocks.zh: 假設你的藥廠位於台灣中部，進水 TDS 約 200 ppm，需要同時供應 PW 和 WFI。從 Table 3-1 的選項中，你會優先考慮哪種前處理+純化組合？為什麼？
blocks.en: Suppose your plant is in central Taiwan, with feed water TDS of about 200 ppm, and you need to supply both PW and WFI. From the options in Table 3-1, which pretreatment + purification combination would you consider first, and why?

blocks.zh: 提示：考慮台灣的水質特性（硬度中等、有機物偏高）、化學品管理的複雜性、以及 WFI 的生產方式（蒸餾 vs. 膜法）。
blocks.en: Hint: consider the characteristics of Taiwan's water (moderate hardness, relatively high organics), the complexity of managing chemicals, and how WFI is produced (distillation vs. membrane methods).

blocks.zh: 核心概念：製藥用水的總成本結構
blocks.en: Core Concept: Total Cost Structure of Pharmaceutical Water

blocks.zh: 製藥用水的成本不只是「買設備」那麼簡單，完整成本包含：
blocks.en: The cost of pharmaceutical water is not just "buying equipment". The full cost includes:

blocks.zh: 進水成本（Feed Water）：自來水費用
blocks.en: Feed water cost (Feed Water): municipal water charges

blocks.zh: 前處理成本（Pretreatment）：過濾、軟化、活性碳
blocks.en: Pretreatment cost (Pretreatment): filtration, softening, activated carbon

blocks.zh: 最終處理成本（Final Treatment）：RO、DI、EDI、蒸餾
blocks.en: Final treatment cost (Final Treatment): RO, DI, EDI, distillation

blocks.zh: 驗證成本（Validation）：IQ/OQ/PQ + 持續監控
blocks.en: Validation cost (Validation): IQ/OQ/PQ + ongoing monitoring

blocks.zh: QA/QC 成本：日常取樣、檢測、趨勢分析
blocks.en: QA/QC cost: routine sampling, testing, trend analysis

blocks.zh: 廢水處理成本（Waste Treatment）：排放處理
blocks.en: Waste treatment cost (Waste Treatment): discharge treatment

blocks.zh: 不合規風險成本（Noncompliance Risk）：系統故障、產品報廢
blocks.en: Noncompliance risk cost (Noncompliance Risk): system failure, product loss

blocks.zh: NPV 分析框架
blocks.en: NPV Analysis Framework

blocks.zh:
Total NPV = Capital Cost + Σ (Annual Operating Cost / (1+r)^n)
                n=1 to 5

其中 Operating Cost 包含：
  - 耗材（濾材、樹脂、膜元件更換）
  - 化學品（酸、鹼、鹽、消毒劑）
  - 能源（電力、蒸汽）
  - 人工（操作、維護、取樣檢測）
  - 水費（進水 + 排水）
blocks.en:
Total NPV = Capital Cost + Σ (Annual Operating Cost / (1+r)^n)
                n=1 to 5

where Operating Cost includes:
  - Consumables (filter media, resin, membrane element replacement)
  - Chemicals (acids, bases, salt, sanitizing agents)
  - Energy (electricity, steam)
  - Labor (operation, maintenance, sampling and testing)
  - Water charges (feed water + discharge)

blocks.zh: 關鍵結論：不同水處理系統的 NPV 其實相差不大，但 Membrane-Based Systems（膜系統，如 RO/EDI）的 NPV 略低，這也是它成為主流的原因之一。
blocks.en: Key conclusion: the NPVs of the different water treatment systems are in fact fairly close, but Membrane-Based Systems (e.g. RO/EDI) have a slightly lower NPV, which is one reason they became the mainstream choice.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：五年分析期的意義
blocks.en: Key Point: Why a Five-Year Analysis Period

blocks.zh: 為什麼是五年？因為需要一個夠長的期間讓運營成本成為顯著因素（與資本支出比較），但又不能太長以至於預測失準。
blocks.en: Why five years? The period must be long enough for operating costs to become a significant factor (compared with capital expenditure), but not so long that the forecasts become unreliable.

blocks.zh: 例外情況：非再生型混合床（Off-site Regenerated DI）的 NPV 明顯偏高，因為瓶裝樹脂的更換和外送再生費用會隨時間快速累積。
blocks.en: Exception: the NPV of non-regenerable mixed beds (Off-site Regenerated DI) is clearly higher, because the cost of replacing bottled resin and shipping it out for regeneration accumulates quickly over time.

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：買車 vs. 租車
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: Buying vs. Leasing a Car

blocks.zh: NPV 分析就像比較「買車 vs. 租車」：
blocks.en: NPV analysis is like comparing "buying vs. leasing a car":

blocks.zh: 蒸餾系統 = 買一台高級車（資本成本高、維護費穩定）
blocks.en: Distillation system = buying a premium car (high capital cost, stable maintenance cost)

blocks.zh: RO/EDI 系統 = 買一台省油車（資本成本中等、運營成本最低）
blocks.en: RO/EDI system = buying a fuel-efficient car (moderate capital cost, lowest operating cost)

blocks.zh: 外送再生 DI = 長期租車（初期便宜但五年下來最貴）
blocks.en: Off-site regenerated DI = a long-term lease (cheap at first but the most expensive after five years)

blocks.zh: CDMO 實務：廢水回收的隱藏價值
blocks.en: CDMO Practice: The Hidden Value of Wastewater Recovery

blocks.zh: 原文提到廢水可用於灌溉、加濕、鍋爐補水等。在台灣的 CDMO 環境中，更實際的回收途徑：
blocks.en: The source text mentions that wastewater can be used for irrigation, humidification, boiler make-up and so on. In a Taiwan CDMO setting, more practical recovery routes are:

blocks.zh: RO 排水（Reject Water）回收率可達 75-85%，剩餘的 15-25% 可用於冷卻塔補水
blocks.en: RO reject water recovery can reach 75-85%, and the remaining 15-25% can be used as cooling tower make-up

blocks.zh: 初始沖洗水可用於前處理系統的反洗
blocks.en: Initial rinse water can be used for backwashing the pretreatment system

blocks.zh: 在水資源日益緊張的地區（如台灣中南部），廢水回收可以成為環評的加分項
blocks.en: In regions where water resources are increasingly tight (such as central and southern Taiwan), wastewater recovery can be a plus point in the environmental impact assessment

blocks.zh: 關鍵警語：水系統是藥廠最貴的原料/公用設施
blocks.en: Key Warning: The Water System Is the Most Expensive Raw Material/Utility in a Drug Plant

blocks.zh: 原文直接說明：高純度水和蒸汽是藥廠中 使用最廣、成本最高的原料或公用設施。系統選型錯誤的後果：
blocks.en: The source text states directly that high-purity water and steam are the most widely used and most costly raw materials or utilities in a pharmaceutical plant. The consequences of selecting the wrong system:

blocks.zh: Under-sized（偏小） → 限制產能甚至停產
blocks.en: Under-sized → limits capacity or even stops production

blocks.zh: Over-sized（偏大） → 品質不穩定（水滯留）+ 資本浪費
blocks.en: Over-sized → unstable quality (stagnant water) + wasted capital

blocks.zh: 但重點是：系統大小不是設計的起點 — 先定義水質需求和用量，再決定系統規模。
blocks.en: But the main point is: system size is not the starting point of design - first define the water quality requirements and demand, then decide the system size.

blocks.zh: 核心概念：三大系統邊界（Figure 3-2）
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Three System Boundaries (Figure 3-2)

blocks.zh: ISPE 的水系統規劃方法論圍繞三個 Primary Boundaries（主要邊界）：
blocks.en: ISPE's water system planning methodology revolves around three Primary Boundaries:

blocks.zh: Water Quality（水質） — 需要什麼等級的水？
blocks.en: Water Quality - what grade of water is needed?

blocks.zh: Use-Point Criteria（使用點標準） — 每個用水點的壓力、流量、溫度需求？
blocks.en: Use-Point Criteria - what are the pressure, flow and temperature requirements at each point of use?

blocks.zh: System Criteria（系統標準） — 儲存、生成、配送的整體設計？
blocks.en: System Criteria - the overall design of storage, generation and distribution

blocks.zh: 每個邊界都有三層概念：
blocks.en: Each boundary has three layers of concept:

blocks.zh: Boundaries（邊界）：不可逾越的底線（如法規要求）
blocks.en: Boundaries: lines that cannot be crossed (e.g. regulatory requirements)

blocks.zh: Limitations（限制）：操作範圍和策略（如可接受的範圍）
blocks.en: Limitations: operating ranges and strategies (e.g. acceptable ranges)

blocks.zh: Restrictions（約束）：現實條件的強制限制（如現有設備、空間）
blocks.en: Restrictions: mandatory constraints imposed by real-world conditions (e.g. existing equipment, space)

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：蓋房子的三道關卡
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: Three Checkpoints in Building a House

blocks.zh: 規劃水系統就像蓋房子：
blocks.en: Planning a water system is like building a house:

blocks.zh: Water Quality = 建築法規（必須達到的標準，不可妥協）
blocks.en: Water Quality = building codes (the standard that must be met, non-negotiable)

blocks.zh: Use-Point Criteria = 住戶需求（每間房要幾個水龍頭、什麼溫度的水）
blocks.en: Use-Point Criteria = residents' needs (how many taps each room needs and at what water temperature)

blocks.zh: System Criteria = 工程規劃（水塔大小、管線配置、水泵選型）
blocks.en: System Criteria = engineering plan (size of the water tower, pipe layout, pump selection)

blocks.zh: 這三者相互影響，需要反覆迭代才能達到最佳方案。
blocks.en: These three influence one another, and several iterations are needed to reach the best solution.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：範圍 vs. 固定值
blocks.en: Key Point: Ranges vs. Fixed Values

blocks.zh: 原文特別強調：文件記載限制條件時，應使用 ranges of acceptability（可接受範圍）而非固定值。這個原則在實務中非常重要：
blocks.en: The source text specifically stresses that when documenting limitations, ranges of acceptability should be used rather than fixed values. This principle is very important in practice:

blocks.zh: 寫「溫度 70-80°C」比寫「溫度 75°C」好 — 給後續設計更多彈性
blocks.en: Writing "temperature 70-80°C" is better than "temperature 75°C" - it gives later design more flexibility

blocks.zh: 寫「電導率 ≤ 1.3 μS/cm」比寫「電導率 0.5 μS/cm」好 — 避免過度設計
blocks.en: Writing "conductivity ≤ 1.3 μS/cm" is better than "conductivity 0.5 μS/cm" - it avoids over-design

blocks.zh: 這與 Chapter 2 的 Design Range / Operating Range 概念完全一致。
blocks.en: This is fully consistent with the Design Range / Operating Range concept in Chapter 2.

blocks.zh: Step 1：確定水質需求
blocks.en: Step 1: Define Water Quality Requirements

blocks.zh: 這是四步驟方法論的第一步。水質選擇的核心考量：
blocks.en: This is the first step of the four-step methodology. The core considerations in choosing water quality are:

blocks.zh: Dosage Form（劑型）：注射劑 → WFI；口服液 → PW 或 Non-compendial
blocks.en: Dosage Form: injectables → WFI; oral liquids → PW or Non-compendial

blocks.zh: Microbial Criteria（微生物標準）：無菌製劑需要嚴格的生物負荷控制
blocks.en: Microbial Criteria: sterile products require strict bioburden control

blocks.zh: Chemical Purity（化學純度）：高濃縮製程需要更低的 TOC 和電導率
blocks.en: Chemical Purity: highly concentrated processes require lower TOC and conductivity

blocks.zh: 實務技巧：做好筆記！
blocks.en: Practical Tip: Take Good Notes!

blocks.zh: 原文建議在指定每個使用點的水質時，同步做筆記記錄決策依據。這不是隨便說說的 — 這些筆記在後續階段有三大用途：
blocks.en: When specifying the water quality for each use point, the source text recommends recording the rationale for each decision at the same time. This is not a casual suggestion - these notes serve three major purposes in later stages:

blocks.zh: 追溯性（Traceability）：審計時能解釋每個水質選擇的理由
blocks.en: Traceability: during audits you can explain the reasoning behind each water quality choice

blocks.zh: 挑戰性（Challengeability）：如果後續系統設計受限，可以回頭重新評估水質要求
blocks.en: Challengeability: if the system design is later constrained, you can go back and re-evaluate the water quality requirement

blocks.zh: 知識管理：新專案可以參考過往的決策邏輯
blocks.en: Knowledge management: new projects can refer to the decision logic of past ones

blocks.zh: Step 2：特徵化使用點
blocks.en: Step 2: Characterize the Use Points

blocks.zh: 第二步是為每個用水點建立詳細的需求矩陣，包含三個核心參數：
blocks.en: The second step is to build a detailed requirements matrix for each point of use, covering three core parameters:

blocks.zh: Pressure（壓力） — 用水點所需的最低供水壓力
blocks.en: Pressure - the minimum supply pressure required at the use point

blocks.zh: Flow（流量） — 瞬時流量（LPM）和每日用量（LPD）
blocks.en: Flow - instantaneous flow (LPM) and daily consumption (LPD)

blocks.zh: Temperature Range（溫度範圍） — 進水溫度的可接受範圍
blocks.en: Temperature Range - the acceptable range of supply water temperature

blocks.zh: 注意：同樣強調 range（範圍）而非 fixed value（固定值）。
blocks.en: Note: again the emphasis is on a range rather than a fixed value.

blocks.zh: 關鍵概念：Diversity Factor（多樣性因子）
blocks.en: Key Concept: Diversity Factor

blocks.zh: Diversity Factor 是水系統設計中非常實用的概念：
blocks.en: The Diversity Factor is a very practical concept in water system design:

blocks.zh: 值 = 1：該設備會在設計情境中使用
blocks.en: Value = 1: the equipment will be in use in the design scenario

blocks.zh: 值 = 0：該設備在該時段不會同時使用
blocks.en: Value = 0: the equipment will not be in use at the same time during that period

blocks.zh: 以 Table 3-2 為例：CIP 和 Stopper Washer 不會同時用水，所以瞬時流量只取較大值（40 LPM），但每日用水量兩者都要算（1200 + 460 = 1660 LPD）。
blocks.en: Taking Table 3-2 as an example: CIP and the Stopper Washer will not draw water at the same time, so the instantaneous flow takes only the larger value (40 LPM), but the daily consumption of both must be counted (1200 + 460 = 1660 LPD).

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：Diversity Factor = 電梯容量設計
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: Diversity Factor = Elevator Capacity Design

blocks.zh: 就像一棟 20 層樓的辦公大樓，不會所有員工同時搭電梯。Diversity Factor 就是估算「同時使用率」的工具：
blocks.en: In a 20-story office building, not all employees take the elevator at the same moment. The Diversity Factor is the tool for estimating this "simultaneous use rate":

blocks.zh: 流量的 Diversity：就像「尖峰時段同時等電梯的人數」→ 決定管線大小
blocks.en: Diversity of flow: like "the number of people waiting for the elevator at peak time" → determines pipe size

blocks.zh: 日用量的 Diversity：就像「一天的總搭乘人次」→ 決定水箱和產水設備的大小
blocks.en: Diversity of daily consumption: like "the total number of rides in a day" → determines the size of the tank and the generation equipment

blocks.zh: 重點提示：兩個不同用途的數字
blocks.en: Key Point: Two Numbers for Two Different Purposes

blocks.zh: Flowrate（瞬時流量） → 用來決定 管線尺寸（Line Sizing）
blocks.en: Flowrate (instantaneous flow) → used to determine Line Sizing

blocks.zh: Daily Use（每日用量） → 用來決定 儲存容量（Storage）和產水能力（Generation）
blocks.en: Daily Use → used to determine Storage and Generation capacity

blocks.zh: 混淆這兩者是新手常犯的錯誤。管線設計看的是「最大同時流量」，而儲存和產水看的是「一天的總消耗量」。
blocks.en: Confusing the two is a common beginner's mistake. Piping design looks at the "maximum simultaneous flow", while storage and generation look at the "total consumption in a day".

blocks.zh: 一條無菌充填線有以下用水設備：
blocks.en: An aseptic filling line has the following water-using equipment:

blocks.zh: 配液罐清洗（CIP）：50 LPM，每批使用 2000 L，每天 2 批
blocks.en: Compounding tank cleaning (CIP): 50 LPM, 2000 L per batch, 2 batches per day

blocks.zh: 膠塞清洗機：15 LPM，每批使用 600 L，每天 1 批
blocks.en: Stopper washer: 15 LPM, 600 L per batch, 1 batch per day

blocks.zh: 充填機沖洗：5 LPM，每批使用 200 L，每天 3 批
blocks.en: Filling machine rinse: 5 LPM, 200 L per batch, 3 batches per day

blocks.zh: CIP 和膠塞清洗不會同時運行
blocks.en: CIP and the stopper washer do not run at the same time

blocks.zh: 請計算：(1) Design Flowrate for loop sizing? (2) Total daily demand?
blocks.en: Calculate: (1) Design Flowrate for loop sizing? (2) Total daily demand?

blocks.zh: Step 3：建立系統標準
blocks.en: Step 3: Establish System Criteria

blocks.zh: 第三步是利用前兩步收集的數據，透過分析工具來建立系統的整體設計標準：
blocks.en: The third step uses the data gathered in the first two steps and applies analytical tools to establish the overall design criteria for the system:

blocks.zh: Histogram Analysis（直方圖分析） — 繪製 24 小時用水曲線，找出尖峰和低谷
blocks.en: Histogram Analysis - plot the 24-hour water usage curve to identify peaks and troughs

blocks.zh: Storage Tank Profile（儲水槽液位曲線） — 模擬不同情境下的水位變化
blocks.en: Storage Tank Profile - simulate the change in tank level under different scenarios

blocks.zh: Failure Recovery Simulation（故障恢復模擬） — 系統故障時能撐多久
blocks.en: Failure Recovery Simulation - how long the system can last when a failure occurs

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：水塔設計 = 行動電源容量
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: Water Tower Design = Power Bank Capacity

blocks.zh: 設計儲水系統就像選行動電源：
blocks.en: Designing a water storage system is like choosing a power bank:

blocks.zh: 尖峰需求 = 你用手機最耗電的時段（看影片、打遊戲）
blocks.en: Peak demand = the period when your phone drains fastest (watching video, playing games)

blocks.zh: 平均需求 = 一天的正常使用量
blocks.en: Average demand = normal usage over a day

blocks.zh: Recovery Time = 行動電源充回滿電需要多久
blocks.en: Recovery Time = how long it takes to recharge the power bank fully

blocks.zh: 儲水槽大小 = 行動電源容量（太小會不夠用，太大則笨重浪費）
blocks.en: Tank size = power bank capacity (too small is not enough, too large is bulky and wasteful)

blocks.zh: 沒有固定的「最佳水位」，要根據你的實際使用模式來決定。
blocks.en: There is no fixed "best water level"; it must be decided from your actual usage pattern.

blocks.zh: 七個必問問題（System Restrictions Checklist）
blocks.en: Seven Must-Ask Questions (System Restrictions Checklist)

blocks.zh: 這七個問題是系統設計的「現實檢查」，每一個都可能改變你的設計方向：
blocks.en: These seven questions are a "reality check" for system design, and each one may change your design direction:

blocks.zh: 24/7 可用性？ → 是否需要備援系統
blocks.en: 24/7 availability? → is a backup system needed

blocks.zh: 停機限制？ → 影響維護和消毒排程
blocks.en: Downtime restrictions? → affects maintenance and sanitization scheduling

blocks.zh: 化學品處理能力？ → 決定是否能用再生型 DI（需要酸鹼）
blocks.en: Chemical handling capability? → determines whether regenerable DI (requiring acid and base) can be used

blocks.zh: 批次 vs. 連續？ → 影響尖峰流量和儲存需求
blocks.en: Batch vs. continuous? → affects peak flow and storage requirements

blocks.zh: 專用 vs. 多產品？ → 多產品需考慮不同水質需求
blocks.en: Dedicated vs. multi-product? → multi-product operation must consider different water quality needs

blocks.zh: 產品切換（Campaigning）？ → 切換間是否需要完整沖洗
blocks.en: Product changeover (Campaigning)? → is a full flush needed between changeovers

blocks.zh: 消毒時間？ → 是否需要冗餘設備以確保消毒不影響供水
blocks.en: Sanitization time? → is redundant equipment needed so that sanitization does not interrupt supply

blocks.zh: CDMO 實務：多產品切換的水系統挑戰
blocks.en: CDMO Practice: Water System Challenges of Multi-Product Changeover

blocks.zh: 對 CDMO 來說，問題 5-7 特別關鍵：
blocks.en: For a CDMO, questions 5-7 are especially critical:

blocks.zh: 多客戶產品 → 不同客戶可能對水質有不同的額外要求
blocks.en: Multi-client products → different clients may have different additional water quality requirements

blocks.zh: Campaigning → 產品切換時的水系統清洗驗證（Cleaning Validation）是重要議題
blocks.en: Campaigning → cleaning validation of the water system at product changeover is an important topic

blocks.zh: 消毒冗餘 → 無菌充填 CDMO 的水系統通常需要 Hot Water Sanitization（熱水消毒），需要預留時間窗口，可能需要備援迴路
blocks.en: Sanitization redundancy → the water system of an aseptic filling CDMO usually needs Hot Water Sanitization, which requires a reserved time window and may require a backup loop

blocks.zh: Step 4：重新檢視水質
blocks.en: Step 4: Revisit Water Quality

blocks.zh: 這是四步驟方法論的最後一步，也是最容易被忽略的一步。經過前三步的分析後，你可能發現：
blocks.en: This is the last step of the four-step methodology, and the one most easily overlooked. After the analysis in the first three steps, you may find that:

blocks.zh: 某些使用點的水質需求可以合併（減少系統複雜度）
blocks.en: The water quality requirements of some use points can be merged (reducing system complexity)

blocks.zh: 某些使用點可以接受更高品質的水（用 WFI 取代 PW，統一系統）
blocks.en: Some use points can accept a higher quality of water (replacing PW with WFI to unify the system)

blocks.zh: 某些使用點的用量可以調整（限制尖峰需求）
blocks.en: The consumption of some use points can be adjusted (limiting peak demand)

blocks.zh: 關鍵原則：Compromise（妥協）是必然的
blocks.en: Key Principle: Compromise Is Inevitable

blocks.zh: 原文用了 “compromises must be made” 這個非常務實的說法。在實際規劃中，常見的妥協策略包括：
blocks.en: The source text uses the very pragmatic phrase "compromises must be made". In real planning, common compromise strategies include:

blocks.zh: 升級策略（Upgrade）：全部用高品質水 → 簡化系統，但成本增加
blocks.en: Upgrade strategy: use high-quality water everywhere → simplifies the system but increases cost

blocks.zh: 限流策略（Demand Control）：限制某些使用點的用水量 → 降低尖峰需求
blocks.en: Demand Control strategy: limit the water use of certain use points → lowers peak demand

blocks.zh: 排程策略（Scheduling）：錯開高用水設備的運行時間 → 減小水箱和產水設備
blocks.en: Scheduling strategy: stagger the operating times of high-consumption equipment → smaller tanks and generation equipment

blocks.zh: 無論怎麼妥協，底線是：水質必須在邊界限制之內。
blocks.en: Whatever compromise is made, the bottom line is that water quality must stay within the boundary limits.

blocks.zh: 生活比喻：四步驟 = PDCA 循環
blocks.en: Everyday Analogy: The Four Steps = a PDCA Cycle

blocks.zh: 這四步驟其實就是一個迷你版的 Plan-Do-Check-Act 循環：
blocks.en: These four steps are in effect a mini Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle:

blocks.zh: Plan：確定水質需求（Step 1）
blocks.en: Plan: define water quality requirements (Step 1)

blocks.zh: Do：特徵化使用點（Step 2）
blocks.en: Do: characterize the use points (Step 2)

blocks.zh: Check：建立系統標準、發現限制（Step 3）
blocks.en: Check: establish system criteria and identify restrictions (Step 3)

blocks.zh: Act：重新檢視、做出妥協（Step 4）→ 然後回到 Step 1 再迭代
blocks.en: Act: revisit and make compromises (Step 4) → then return to Step 1 and iterate

blocks.zh: 好的水系統規劃通常會經歷 2-3 輪迭代才能定案。
blocks.en: Good water system planning usually goes through 2-3 iterations before it is finalized.

blocks.zh: 系統設計的核心決策
blocks.en: Core Decisions in System Design

blocks.zh: 進入系統設計階段後，主要需要做出以下決策：
blocks.en: Once in the system design phase, the main decisions to be made are:

blocks.zh: 配送架構：Central Storage（集中儲存）vs. Multiple Loops（多迴路）
blocks.en: Distribution architecture: Central Storage vs. Multiple Loops

blocks.zh: 溫度策略：Hot Distribution（熱配送 ≥70°C）vs. Ambient/Cold（常溫/冷配送）
blocks.en: Temperature strategy: Hot Distribution (≥70°C) vs. Ambient/Cold

blocks.zh: 備援策略：Lead-Lag Operation（主備切換）vs. N+1 Redundancy（冗餘設備）
blocks.en: Redundancy strategy: Lead-Lag Operation vs. N+1 Redundancy

blocks.zh: 規模策略：One Large System vs. Multiple Small Systems
blocks.en: Scale strategy: One Large System vs. Multiple Small Systems

blocks.zh: 重點提示：Hot vs. Cold Distribution
blocks.en: Key Point: Hot vs. Cold Distribution

blocks.zh: 溫度策略的選擇直接影響微生物控制方案：
blocks.en: The choice of temperature strategy directly affects the microbial control approach:

blocks.zh: Hot Distribution（≥70°C）：持續抑菌，不需要定期消毒，但能耗高、管材要求高
blocks.en: Hot Distribution (≥70°C): continuously bacteriostatic and needs no periodic sanitization, but energy consumption is high and the piping material requirements are demanding

blocks.zh: Cold/Ambient Distribution：能耗低，但需要定期 Heat Sanitization（熱消毒）
blocks.en: Cold/Ambient Distribution: low energy consumption, but requires periodic Heat Sanitization

blocks.zh: 關鍵限制：如果工廠是 24/7 運作，冷系統可能沒有時間窗口進行熱消毒 → 被迫選擇熱配送
blocks.en: Key restriction: if the plant runs 24/7, a cold system may have no time window for heat sanitization → hot distribution is forced

blocks.zh: 重點提示：Lead-Lag 備援運行
blocks.en: Key Point: Lead-Lag Redundant Operation

blocks.zh: Lead-Lag Operation（主備切換）是常見的備援策略：
blocks.en: Lead-Lag Operation is a common redundancy strategy:

blocks.zh: Lead（主設備）：正常運行
blocks.en: Lead (duty equipment): runs normally

blocks.zh: Lag（備用設備）：待命狀態，主設備故障時自動接手
blocks.en: Lag (standby equipment): on standby and takes over automatically if the duty equipment fails

blocks.zh: 也可以輪替使用，確保兩台設備都保持在良好狀態
blocks.en: The two can also be rotated so that both units stay in good condition

blocks.zh: 特別適用於蒸餾器、RO 膜組等關鍵設備
blocks.en: Particularly suitable for critical equipment such as stills and RO membrane skids

blocks.zh: CDMO 實務：系統設計的特殊考量
blocks.en: CDMO Practice: Special Considerations in System Design

blocks.zh: 對無菌充填 CDMO 而言，系統設計還需額外考量：
blocks.en: For an aseptic filling CDMO, system design needs some additional considerations:

blocks.zh: 客戶審計期望：大型藥廠客戶通常偏好 Hot WFI Loop（熱 WFI 迴路），因為這是業界「黃金標準」
blocks.en: Client audit expectations: large pharmaceutical clients usually prefer a Hot WFI Loop, as it is the industry "gold standard"

blocks.zh: 未來擴展：CDMO 業務增長快速，預留 30-50% 擴充能力是常見做法
blocks.en: Future expansion: CDMO businesses grow quickly, and reserving 30-50% expansion capacity is common practice

blocks.zh: 多棟建築：如果有多條充填線分布在不同潔淨區，需要考慮是集中供水還是分區供水
blocks.en: Multiple buildings: if several filling lines are spread across different clean areas, consider whether to supply centrally or by zone

blocks.zh: 備援要求：無菌充填一旦停產損失巨大，建議關鍵設備都有 Lead-Lag 備援
blocks.en: Redundancy requirements: the loss from an aseptic filling stoppage is huge, so Lead-Lag redundancy is recommended for all critical equipment

blocks.zh: 綜合練習
blocks.en: Comprehensive Exercise

blocks.zh: 你正在規劃一座新的 CDMO 無菌充填工廠，有以下條件：
blocks.en: You are planning a new CDMO aseptic filling plant with the following conditions:

blocks.zh: 兩條充填線，分布在同一棟建築的不同樓層
blocks.en: Two filling lines, on different floors of the same building

blocks.zh: 需要 WFI 供應充填、配液、CIP、膠塞清洗
blocks.en: WFI is needed for filling, compounding, CIP and stopper washing

blocks.zh: 工廠 24/7 運作，每週有 8 小時維護窗口
blocks.en: The plant operates 24/7, with an 8-hour maintenance window each week

blocks.zh: 預計三年內增加第三條充填線
blocks.en: A third filling line is expected to be added within three years

blocks.zh: 請根據本章所學，回答以下問題：
blocks.en: Based on what you learned in this chapter, answer the following questions:

blocks.zh: 你會選擇 Central System 還是 Multiple Systems？為什麼？
blocks.en: Would you choose a Central System or Multiple Systems? Why?

blocks.zh: 你會選擇 Hot Distribution 還是 Cold + Periodic Sanitization？為什麼？

blocks.en: What is your redundancy strategy?

blocks.zh: 本節重點摘要 Section Summary
blocks.en: Section Summary

blocks.zh: 水質階層：Drinking Water → Non-Compendial → PW (Compendial) → WFI，選擇依據是產品特性、製程需求和預期用途。非藥典水不等於低品質水。
blocks.en: Water quality hierarchy: Drinking Water → Non-Compendial → PW (Compendial) → WFI; the selection is based on product characteristics, process requirements and intended use. Non-compendial water does not mean low-quality water.

blocks.zh: Decision Tree：Figure 3-1 提供水質選擇的系統化流程，但藥品申請文件中的承諾優先於 Decision Tree。
blocks.en: Decision Tree: Figure 3-1 provides a systematic process for selecting water quality, but commitments in the drug application take precedence over the Decision Tree.

blocks.zh: 成本分析：使用 NPV（五年期）比較不同方案。膜系統（RO/EDI）NPV 最低；不同水處理系統的 NPV 差異其實不大，除了外送再生 DI。
blocks.en: Cost analysis: use NPV (five-year period) to compare options. Membrane systems (RO/EDI) have the lowest NPV; the NPV differences between water treatment systems are in fact small, except for off-site regenerated DI.

blocks.zh: 四步驟規劃法：(1) 確定水質 → (2) 特徵化使用點 → (3) 建立系統標準 → (4) 重新檢視水質。這是一個迭代過程，通常需要 2-3 輪。
blocks.en: Four-step planning method: (1) define water quality → (2) characterize the use points → (3) establish system criteria → (4) revisit water quality. This is an iterative process, usually taking 2-3 rounds.

blocks.zh: Diversity Factor：用來估算同時使用率，瞬時流量決定管線尺寸，每日用量決定儲存和產水能力。
blocks.en: Diversity Factor: used to estimate simultaneous use; instantaneous flow determines pipe size, and daily consumption determines storage and generation capacity.

blocks.zh: 系統設計：Central vs. Multiple Systems、Hot vs. Cold Distribution、Lead-Lag Backup 是三大核心決策。所有妥協都必須在邊界限制之內。
blocks.en: System design: Central vs. Multiple Systems, Hot vs. Cold Distribution, and Lead-Lag Backup are the three core decisions. All compromises must stay within the boundary limits.
